record.title: Baidu releases Unlimited OCR 2 with open weights and long-document parsing claims
record.summary: Baidu announced the October 27 release of Unlimited OCR 2 and made model weights and code available through its official repository. The repository describes sparse reference sliding-window attention (SR-SWA), which limits text-visual attention to a fixed working-reference set, and includes an evaluation runner for MPDocBench and MarathonDocBench. Baidu reports scores of 84.6 and 77.1 on those benchmarks and says the model parsed more than 3,600 pages in one request. These are vendor-reported results; this review did not reproduce them or audit the full benchmark protocol.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Baidu’s Chinese-language announcement and official repository record the October 27 release of Unlimited OCR 2 and make model/code resources publicly accessible.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The repository describes sparse reference sliding-window attention (SR-SWA), which reduces long-sequence text-visual attention interactions to a fixed-size working-reference set.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Baidu reports scores of 84.6 on MPDocBench and 77.1 on MarathonDocBench, and says the model parsed more than 3,600 pages in one request. These results were not independently reproduced in this activation.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: Broad accuracy, comparative superiority, reliable unbounded document length and performance outside the reported evaluation setup are not established by this review.

evidence_gaps.description: The reported benchmark scores and multi-thousand-page example have not been independently reproduced with pinned model weights and matched baselines.
This activation did not audit the full evaluation protocol or characterize error rates as page count and document domain vary.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported long-document parsing mechanism and quality generalize, open weights and code could expand practical document OCR to much longer inputs; the current vendor claims do not establish broad accuracy or independent reproduction.
limitations: Benchmark scores and the long-book example are reported by Baidu and were not reproduced here.
The repository is on mutable main; this activation did not pin weights or code to immutable revisions.
The full benchmark datasets, scoring protocol and comparison conditions were not audited.
A release and public evaluation runner do not establish reliable performance on arbitrary document lengths or domains.
brief.summary: Baidu announced the October 27 release of Unlimited OCR 2 and made model weights and code available through its official repository. The repository describes sparse reference sliding-window attention (SR-SWA), which limits text-visual attention to a fixed working-reference set, and includes an evaluation runner for MPDocBench and MarathonDocBench. Baidu reports scores of 84.6 and 77.1 on those benchmarks and says the model parsed more than 3,600 pages in one request. technical.claimed_result: Baidu reports that Unlimited OCR 2 parses documents beyond prior page limits and reports 84.6 on MPDocBench and 77.1 on MarathonDocBench, along with a >3,600-page example.
technical.demonstrated_result: The dated release announcement and public code/model resources are directly observable. This activation did not run inference or reproduce the reported results.
technical.mechanism: The official repository describes sparse reference sliding-window attention (SR-SWA), which compresses text-visual attention interactions into a fixed working-reference set, and documents one-request multi-page inference.
technical.regime: Vendor-reported long-document OCR and parsing; the evaluation protocol and practical maximum reliable length were not independently assessed.
technical.reproducibility: The official repository includes inference instructions and evaluation scripts, but the model revision and datasets were not pinned and no benchmark was run in this activation.
technical.strongest_baseline: Baidu compares against named commercial models in its announcement; matched conditions and independent comparative results were not established.

brief.title: Baidu releases Unlimited OCR 2 with open weights and long-document parsing claims
brief.why_it_matters: An openly released document-parsing model paired with a bounded-attention mechanism could make long-document OCR more accessible. The practical accuracy, page-length behavior and comparative scores require independent evaluation.
